notes.summary: BJ supplies the genuine singular mixed E1 operator, exact mass and energy, target energy criterion, comparison and uniqueness. Existence and onto normalization remain conditional on genuine envelopes.
notes.detailedSummary: The actual general-variety scope of BJ1801.08229v4 includes reduced irreducible singular and nonnormal projective varieties over algebraically closed trivially valued fields and ample real numerical Cartier classes. Its operator construction precedes envelopes. Raw diagonal mass is V, normalized MA is a probability, and E(phi+c)=E(phi)+c. Finite dual energy is equivalent to all-E1 integrability. EP is equivalent to surjectivity and completeness, but this does not establish singular geometrically unibranch EP.
notes.text:
Primary-source partial theorem. Retain k algebraically closed, trivially valued and characteristic zero, X reduced irreducible projective, and omega any ample real numerical Cartier class, including every ample line bundle. Put V=(omega^n)>0. BJ Section 7 returns to general varieties after its smooth-only subsection; Theorem 12.8 has general irreducible scope. The sufficient envelope theorem 5.20 and equation theorem 12.9 have smooth hypotheses.

Relative integral closure of configurations is taken in their prescribed generic fiber. Absolute normalization would change a nonnormal X. BJ1.13 supplies vertical DVRs. For central components E, b_E=ord_E(t) and v_E=b_E^(-1)ord_E. The genuine mixed model measure is sum_E b_E product_i((omega_i,model+D_i)|E) delta_vE. Relative nefness gives nonnegative weights and the central-fiber intersection cycle gives mass (omega_1...omega_n).

Compactified intersection extends by decreasing model majorants and is finite on mixed E1 tuples. Its multilinear extension defines Radon measures through integral h M=pairing((0,h),(omega_1,phi_1),...,(omega_n,phi_n)). Positivity bounds the functional by mass times sup norm; PL density and Radon representation give existence and uniqueness. BJ7.19 proves actual model agreement, mass, mixed integrability, decreasing continuity and normalization pushforward. Weighted and strong continuity have their primary-source theorems. This constructs the genuine operator before equation surjectivity.

The actual energy is E(phi)=pairing((omega,phi)^(n+1))/((n+1)V), with E(0)=0 and E(phi+c)=E(phi)+c. Raw diagonal MA has mass V; probability MA=raw/V. Global locality gives comparison integral_{phi<psi} MA(psi)<=integral_{phi<psi} MA(phi). With I=integral (phi-psi)(MA(psi)-MA(phi)), equal measures give I=0. Divisorial finite-dual-energy Dirac tests and minimal usc divisorial extension prove uniqueness modulo one constant. Global domination likewise precedes EP.

For a raw positive Radon target nu, its mass must be V. With mu=nu/V, the exact energy condition is sup_{psi in E1}(E(psi)-integral psi mu)<infinity. BJ9.20 proves equivalence with integrability of every E1 potential. The weighted-sum contradiction bounds integration on bounded-J sets; I(t psi,0)<=t[1-(1-t)^n]I(psi,0)<=n t^2 I(psi,0) supplies the scaling estimate. Necessity for solutions follows from the energy tangent inequality. This criterion alone does not prove solvability.

Under genuine EP, general BJ5.11 supplies normalized PSH compactness. Uniform two-sided differentiation, bounded-J target L1 convergence and energy usc give variational attainment; testing both signs gives the constructed MA equation. The raw objective is VE-integral phi nu. Conversely surjectivity/completeness gives envelopes, as BJ12.8 states. Thus the exact arbitrary-support existence theorem remains conditional here.

Normalization pullback preserves energy and pushes genuine mixed measures forward. Onto PSH separately requires BJ5.13's approaching larger classes with EP; onto E1 and target correspondence depend on that descent. A normalization analytic homeomorphism is insufficient.

notes.summary: Determinant traces meet the actual affine FS generator condition, and global FS tests determine nonflat slicing weights. Radial trace equality retains an explicit curve-positivity antecedent.
notes.detailedSummary: Weighted Gauss multiplicativity, Artinian dimensions and dominated generator branches prove the finite-flat FS trace independently of projective norm-metric citations. Generic field-norm coefficients extend over the normal affine-space target, fixing slicing weights through actual FS tests. Trace base change holds for any pulled-back function. The radial argument checks nontrivial scalar extension, Wanner's smooth proper scope, disk comparison, ramification degree and minus-infinity cases. General corrected tropical-image local positivity and the preceding smooth weak trace extension remain unproved.
notes.text:
Independent proof drafts in P16.1-argument.md Sections 4–6. For integral affine A and reduced finite locally free B/A of rank d, the analytic fiber decomposes into local Artinian algebras B_s,y. The correct weight is m_y=dim_H(s) B_s,y, retaining nilpotents and residue degrees; sum m_y=d.

For actual affine FS u=max(lambda,c_i log|f_i|+C_i), clear positive rational coefficients by D. Set b_0=1, b_i=f_i^(D c_i), w_0=D lambda and w_i=D C_i. The basis-independent determinant P(T)=det(mult_(sum T_i b_i))=sum a_beta T^beta has coefficients in A, even when B is locally free but not globally free. After algebraically closed extension, Artinian composition series give P=product_x(sum T_i b_i(x))^length_x. Weighted Gauss norms are multiplicative at every positive real radius: lexicographically largest maximal terms have a unique maximal product contribution. Scalar extension preserves coefficient norms. Therefore N(u)=max_beta(D^(-1)log|a_beta|+D^(-1)sum beta_i w_i), with floor d lambda.

The coefficients need not generate A. Polynomial expressions for base generators g_j in the source generators give global rational bounds u>=eta_j log|g_j compose pi|-M_j, eta_j>0. Consequently N(u)>=d eta_j log|g_j|-dM_j. Adding these dominated branches leaves the value unchanged and supplies the exact affine FS generator condition. Fixed finite fiber sums preserve decreasing limits; trace generic finiteness remains a separate check. Continuous finite limits give continuous traces by compact uniform convergence and the error bound d times the source error.

For a=z^2 and u=max(log|z|,-1), P=T_0^2-aT_1^2 gives N(u)=max(-2,log|a|). At a=0 the length-two nilpotent fiber contributes -2. Split points or one degree-two residue field give the same formula away from zero. An unweighted point count would be incorrect.

Trace base change needs no regularization: tensor each original Artinian factor with the new completed residue field. Its refined local dimensions sum to the original dimension, and refined points restrict to the original point. This proves the weighted trace identity for every pulled-back function.

For finite integral Y->S with S an affine-space open over the retained k, generic field-norm coefficients are regular: they are integral over normal A[T] and lie in its fraction-polynomial ring. The determinant maximum therefore extends every global FS test trace through the nonflat locus as an actual FS function. Normalize a line preimage through an H(s)-rational lift, generically inside an etale open. Height bounds and finiteness make its components curves; normalization gives smooth finite-flat curves of total degree d. Their positive fiber dimensions yield slicing weights totaling d.

Radial equality for global FS tests gives identical weighted sums for every slicing choice. Differences of actual FS functions form a rational vector lattice, contain rational constants and separate the finite analytic fiber by truncated log norms with dominated generator branches. Their restrictions are dense in all functions on that finite set, forcing equality of individual weights. Thus the weights are independent of line, etale open and tested input. At nonflat fibers they are normalized slicing degrees, not necessarily dimensions of the original nonflat fiber algebra.

The curve equality has explicit analytic hypotheses. Extend F to complete algebraically closed nontrivially valued Omega; for trivial F first use F((T)). Wanner1801.04713v3 Section4 additionally assumes a smooth proper curve. Smooth projective compactifications verify this scope, and the theorem is applied only on open subsets. Continuous ambient-convex PL approximants have positive CLD currents; Thuillier3.1.8(ii) passes decreasing limits to subharmonic functions or identically minus infinity.

Disk comparison gives b(center)<=b(boundary Gauss), and usc gives convergence along those boundary points. This is not an ordinary punctured-neighborhood limit. Locally t=c z^e U(z); residue characteristic zero gives |e|=1 and convergent unit roots, yielding t=c y^e. A target Gauss point has one source Gauss point per disk, with actual fiber degree e: after scaling, Y^e=alpha T is Eisenstein over the rational-function residue field. Properness excludes other preimages near the center. Finite weighted radial sums converge, including minus-infinity cases because the other terms are locally bounded above.

For weak inputs, choose the line after shrinking the open where the birational witness is an isomorphism. Properness extends each generic lift over the normalized curve DVRs; the previously fixed weights remain input-independent. If these curve restrictions after Omega have continuous CLD-psh approximants and the open trace already has a globally regularizable extension, radial equality identifies its center value with the fixed trace. Full compatibility of Wu's corrected tropical-image local class and the preceding smooth weak extension are not proved here. No arbitrary-H(s) affine regularization theorem is asserted.

notes.summary: Algebraic collars are genuine rational model PL; explicit local weights give model nefness. Hartogs coefficient regularization, direct entropy supports and nonnormal pole-order bounds are proved within their stated domains.
notes.detailedSummary: The collar formula checks clipped section norms, signed coefficients, uniform thresholds and the entire boundary divisor. CLD residual degrees apply to the represented singular model without a smooth BFJ equivalence. A common shell handles an entire already-regularizable FS tail. Hartogs coefficients satisfy these algebraic hypotheses when the domain is already Runge. Global simplex approximation, rational series tails and compensated real logarithmic slopes meet the actual FS generator/floor conditions. Localization uses actual pole orders and an f-power conductor. Rossi analytic-piece gluing and the full Runge induction remain separate obligations.
notes.text:
Using n1's genuine global model criterion and decreasing approximation, independent repairs appear in P16.1-argument.md Sections 7–10.

Let g=-log||s_0||_theta>=0 be a proper affine FS exhaustion on an embedding compactification. Write a=max(lambda,q_j log|f_j|+A_j), f_j=F_j/s_0^d_j. Suppose a-cg<=C on the rational shell R<=g<=R+1. Set G=min(g,R+1) and H_j=max(log||F_j||_(d_j theta),-M_j). Choose rational M_j so -q_jM_j+(q_jd_j-c)G+A_j<=C at both endpoints of [0,R+1]. Clipped section norms are differences of actual basepoint-free FS metrics, because their floor branch contains the complete reference system. Thus G,H_j are genuine bounded BJ model PL. The rational PL space is a vector lattice; its real span need not be.

Set A_*=max(C,lambda-cG,{q_jH_j+(q_jd_j-c)G+A_j}) and choose rational K_*>0 with C+K_*>=sup A_*. Then F_*=min(A_*,C+K_*(R+1-G)). The cap is inactive for g<=R; the shell has A_*=C; for g>=R+1, including the whole boundary divisor, the cap is exactly C. This proves the desired algebraic collar representation. It makes no assertion about arbitrary analytic PL.

These constructed local weights are explicit finite convex maxima of algebraic logarithms and have positive CLD curvature. After clearing rational powers, equivariant flag-ideal generators t^(-ell)f show that the formal metric over k((t)) equals the pulled-back metric at every analytic point, not only on the Gauss section. CLD18.8.6 preserves positivity. Reduction and CLD17.7.10 give each integral central curve with its restricted bundle as a residual pre-model; CLD18.8.4 at d=1 gives nonnegative degree. The represented bundle is relatively nef and enters genuine global PSH by BJ's model criterion, retaining its nonnormal generic fiber. No smooth BFJ equivalence is used on a singular quotient.

For a supplied decreasing global FS sequence a_i->u with u<=g+B, select a shell where u-cg<C-1. Nested closed superlevel sets on that compact shell show a whole tail has a_i-cg<C. Collar truncations then decrease globally; genuine closure and sequential FS approximation with complete-system generator/floor branches prove the legitimate already-regularizable extension. This cannot prove arbitrary weak regularization by assuming the sequence being sought.

For an already-Runge Hartogs domain containing the zero section, a strict-margin polynomial polytope exhaustion gives G_j(y,w)=sum_i f_j,i(y)w^i and H_r(y)=max_{j,i>=1}(log|f_j,i(y)|-c_j)/i. These are global regular coefficient expressions. Adding max(H_r,epsilon_r g-r) supplies the rational floor and original generators. Common compact tails and the collar formula give global decreasing FS regularization when -log d_D has upper growth and is nontrivial. Strict opens avoid the false general equality int{|f|<=a}={|f|<a}. The argument does not prove that an arbitrary weak-input Hartogs domain is Runge.

For chi(x)=a^(-1)log(1+sum exp(a x_i)), its entropy-simplex dual has rational face-respecting finite polyhedral approximants with global error e_m=4^(-m), including all infinite-coordinate faces. Rational intercepts preserve vertex zero and single-generator branches. Shifting h_m by 2e_m makes the sequence decreasing. Positive rational series use upper partial sums plus 2^(-N)(v+1). Relative entropy gives unique support contact; compact gap sublevels give uniform separation outside every contact neighborhood.

For s=C+sum alpha_i log|f_i|, choose d_i with log|f_i|<=d_i v, rational q_i,m increasing to alpha_i>0, B_m decreasing from above to sum d_i alpha_i and C_m decreasing to C. Put b_m=B_m-sum d_iq_i,m>0 and s_m=C_m+sum q_i,m log|f_i|+b_mv. Differences are nonnegative sums of d_iv-log|f_i|, so s_m decreases globally. At poles compare shared minus-infinity values without subtraction. H_m=max(s_m,epsilon_m v-m) retains generators and floor and decreases to s. Combining with the remainder-series sequence proves actual global FS supporting membership independently of singular EP.

For localization, assume a log|h|+b<=max(u,-c log|f|)+O(1), h in R_f, and |log|f||<=M on L union {x}, where x is in the original R-polynomial hull. Normalization divisorial rays force a max(-ord_Dh,0)<=c ord_Df. For q/p>c/a, z=h^pf^q is integral over R. A fixed f^N kills R[z]/R, giving z^ell f^N in R. Applying the original hull inequality, letting ell tend to infinity and q/p decrease to c/a yields a log|h(x)|+b<=sup_L(a log|h|+b)+2cM, including zeros and nonnormal algebras. This repairs the false denominator bound for f=z^2,g=z. The complete regularizable localization maximum principle still needs its controlled approximation input.

notes.text:
The original P16.1 and its completion criteria remain unchanged and unproved. n1 supplies genuine global operator, mass, energy, target criterion and uniqueness. n2 supplies determinant traces, fixed slicing weights for actual FS tests and radial equality with explicit post-extension positivity. n3 supplies algebraic collars, already-regularizable extension, already-Runge Hartogs coefficient regularization, direct supports and pole-order localization.

Concrete remaining gates are recorded in status.json and P16.1-argument.md Section 11. Ambient convex smoothing does not establish positivity for every corrected local function specified only on a tropical image. The arbitrary smooth weak upper-growth base still requires compatible bounded local mixed measures, overlap independence, genuine local/global product agreement, mass, integration by parts, comparison and domination. Corrected local extension must retain the actual reference difference and scalar factor: when theta=omega+ddc p, Phi_omega=Psi/A+p and g_omega=v-p+(M+1)/A sum to u/A.

Rossi5.6 and Wu6.15 glue on arbitrary analytic neighborhoods or disjoint analytic pieces outside the narrower global algebraic collar hypotheses. Locally constant integer traces need localization or connectedness to obtain one gamma; gamma=1 needs separate treatment. Complete local projection and Runge induction remain unproved. Therefore weak/global6.5 and the countable rational singular envelope base remain unavailable. Downstream arbitrary-cardinality/real-class singular EP, unconditional existence and onto normalization cannot be claimed. BJ5.13's approaching EP classes remain indispensable for onto PSH/E1 descent.

The genuine nodal obstruction is unconditional. For a rational nodal projective curve with normalization P1 and node preimages p1!=p2, let d=deg L and v=ord_p1. Its Dirac has finite dual energy. Blow up P1 times A1 at (p1,0). The model p*(q*L)+dX0-dE has central degrees 0,d and multiplicities one, hence is nef and has raw measure d delta_v. Its potential has node-preimage endpoint values 0,d. A downstairs E1 solution would pull up with the same target by genuine pushforward, positivity, fixed mass and the unique valuation lift. Upstairs uniqueness forces this potential plus a constant, whereas a downstairs pullback has equal endpoint values. Contradiction.
